A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 4DiM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplied appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original novel-view synthesis experiments, calibration and training-data ablations, temporal-generation results and panorama evaluations in Tables 1–6 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds ZeroNVS comparisons, multi-guidance experiments, frame-interpolation comparisons and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The cascaded diffusion architecture, Masked FiLM, training objective, calibration procedure and multi-guidance equations remain unchanged. Additional architectural and optimizer details document the existing method; revised guidance weights are sampling-setting changes.

E1.justification: V2 explicitly benchmarks DAVIS for video extrapolation and interpolation and adds reflection, lighting and atmospheric examples in Figure 14. The training mixture and principal tasks remain unchanged. Video interpolation/extrapolation already appeared in v1, including a windsurfing example reused among v2's DAVIS-labeled samples, so the coverage extension is limited.

E2.justification: V2 adds ZeroNVS's diffusion model to the RE10K/LLFF comparison in Table 1 and its SDS pipeline to the 360-degree comparison in Appendix G. Appendix H additionally evaluates LDMVFI, FILM and RIFE for frame interpolation. PNVS and MotionCtrl remain in the original NVS comparison.

E3.justification: Reported image/pose/time guidance weights change from 2/4/1 to 1.25/2/2, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. New protocols include controlled guidance sweeps, TSED at threshold 1 and keypoint-distance absolute difference in Figure 7, and matched middle-frame FID evaluation for interpolation. Tables 1–3 drop FVD; existing NVS splits and scene counts remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix B directly tests standard versus separate pose/timestamp guidance and their quality-control tradeoffs. Appendix I extends the existing video co-training ablation with a direct LLFF geometry comparison. Appendices G–H add rotation-only ZeroNVS failure analysis and interpolation artifact comparisons, while Figure 14 supplies challenging visual cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars for experimental performance. Parenthetical table values remain scores on reference images, not uncertainty estimates. The calibration procedure's use of scale variance is also unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds ZeroNVS results, including FID 37.35 on cRE10K and 75.95 on cLLFF. Appendix H reports interpolation FID of 52.89 for 4DiM, 56.28 for LDMVFI, 57.68 for RIFE and 68.88 for FILM. Guidance-sweep and qualitative findings are added. Retained numerical entries in Tables 1–6 are unchanged; Tables 1–3 lose their FVD entries.

T1.justification: The conditional distribution, multi-guidance derivation in Equations 1–3 and SfM alignment mathematics are unchanged. Describing SfM distances as revised metrics in v2 changes their attribution relative to prior work, not their mathematical construction relative to v1. No formal assumptions, theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The principal claims about simultaneous camera/time control and strong NVS performance remain. V2 explicitly claims first-ever metric-scale camera control for NVS, while narrowing the metric contribution from novel SfM distances to fixes of He et al.'s metrics. Keypoint distance remains claimed as novel.

C2.justification: V2 adds focused explanations for ZeroNVS's favorable LLFF reconstruction scores through blur, video co-training's in-domain tradeoff through model capacity, and rotation-only SDS failure through missing parallax. It also qualifies guidance benefits through near-saturated pose accuracy and fidelity/dynamics tradeoffs. The principal stated limitations of 4DiM remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D newly specify architectural block/head counts, channels and convolution kernels, plus Adam learning rate 0.0001, 10,000-step warmup, no learning-rate decay and EMA decay 0.9999. Appendices F–G disclose ZeroNVS scale sweeps and selected settings. These substantially improve implementation documentation, although v1's approximate 2.6B parameter count is removed. Both versions still promise future release of calibrated RE10K.

R1.justification: V2 recasts multi-guidance as a generalization of InstructPix2Pix and SfM distances as modifications to CameraCtrl's evaluation, materially revising attribution of central contributions. Related work also expands to ZeroNVS, frame-interpolation methods and additional camera/video models, and emphasizes geometry-free generation's advantages for dynamics and view-dependent effects.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are rewritten, with further revisions to related-work and experimental explanations, appendix headings and navigation. The main section sequence and most technical exposition remain intact, making this a focused narrative revision rather than a wholesale restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Figure 3, annotates alignment differences in Figure 4, adds guidance plots and comparison/case-study Figures 7–10 and 14, and introduces an interpolation-results table. It also reselects and enlarges supplementary sample grids, relocates existing displays, changes table columns and adopts the conference layout.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked a direct test of multi-guidance and comparative evaluation of temporal interpolation. V2 supplies both in Appendices B and H, adds a relevant NVS comparator, discloses essential implementation details and improves attribution. These changes substantially strengthen validation and reproducibility without relying on higher retained scores. Reporting inconsistencies remain, including Figure 7's TSED threshold 1 versus Appendix E's statement that all experiments use 2, but they do not outweigh these gains.
